newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP demands stricter controls on bathing water.
newsitem.headline: EP demands stricter controls on bathing water.

text.p: The European Parliament called on Thursday for stricter national controls on the quality of bathing water.

Euro-MPs welcomed a European Commission proposal to upate the EU bathing water directive 76/160/EEC -- COM(94)36 -- but called for further cuts in the maximum permitted levels of sewage, chemicals and rubbish.

Of the 18,000 beaches in the EU covered by the Commission's 1995 bathing water report, more than 3,000 either failed to meet EU minimum requirements on clean water or were not monitored closely enough to determine whether they complied.

The Commission is proposing to make it easier for them to comply by dropping from the list of substances which must be monitored those which it deems do not affect bathers' health directly even if they do damage the environment.
These include heavy metals, cyanide, pesticides, ammonia, nitrates and phosphates.
The parliament thought this approach too lax and pushed through amendments obliging the member states to continue monitoring nitrate, phosphate and pesticide levels.
In view of the member states' poor record of compliance with the 1975 directive, Euro-MPs said the public and the Commission should be warned about waters unfit for bathing.

On the advice of rapporteur Doeke Eisma, parliament agreed the quality standards should not just apply to water used for swimming but should cover areas used for sailing, surfing and other water sports.

Eisma recently told Reuters he expected EU environment ministers would reject this demand, but that it might eventually force the Commission to propose separate legislation on water used for recreation other than swimming.
The proposal, given a first reading under the cooperation procedure, is one of two "daughter directives" intended to dovetail with a forthcoming EU framework directive on water policy.
